text.en: A funny poem imagines what would happen if all the laddoos joined into one huge laddoo, all the children into one huge child and all the seas into one huge sea. Then the huge child lifts the huge laddoo and throws it into the huge sea, making a giant splash. In this chapter you will enjoy the poem, think about things that are big, round and floating, match animals with their partners and read about the festival of khichdi.

The poem plays with one idea again and again: what if many small things became one very big thing. It talks about laddoos, children and seas. In each case, many small ones join to make one big one. The word BIG is repeated so that we feel how huge each thing is. At the end the big child throws the big laddoo into the big sea, and the poem ends with a big splish-splash. Splish-splash is a sound word. It copies the sound of water, so we can almost hear it. A poem like this is fun to say aloud in a group, getting louder at each BIG.
A laddoo is round, and many things around us are round, such as a ball, a coin, an orange, a wheel and the moon. Some round things can be eaten, like an orange or a laddoo. Some cannot be eaten, like a ball or a wheel. We can sort them into two columns. Big and small are words that tell us the size of a thing. Describing words like round, sweet, golden and soft tell us about a laddoo. When you describe a thing, think of how it looks, how it feels and how it tastes.
In some words two consonant sounds come together at the start. Both sounds are still there when we say the blend. Pl words are play, plum, plate and plant. Cl words are cloud, clock, clap and clean. Bl words are blue, blanket, black and blow. Make a sentence with each word: I play in the park. The blue blanket is soft. A cloud floats in the sky.
Many animals have a male name and a female name. A cock is a male bird and a hen is the female. A lion is male and a lioness is female. A peacock is male and a peahen is female. A mare is a female horse. A bull is male and a cow is female. A drake is a male duck. To match the pairs, ask: which is the male and which is the female of the same kind of animal?
Some things float on water and some things sink. A dry leaf or feather laid gently on water often stays on the surface. A small piece of dry paper can float at first and may sink after it gets wet. An ordinary stone and a solid metal spoon usually sink. Many wooden pencils float. What a thing is made of and how it is shaped can affect whether it floats. Try this at home with a tub of water, and always have a grown-up near.
Festivals bring people together and help us stay close to nature and culture. Khichdi is cooked with rice and lentils. It is a traditional dish for the harvest festival. Families mark the harvest in different ways. Pongal in Tamil Nadu and Magh Bihu in Assam are harvest celebrations. Sankranti and Lohri are also celebrated around January. Khichdi is one way to cook rice and lentils. Other rice and lentil dishes include savoury pongal in Tamil Nadu and bisi bele bath in Karnataka. Each dish has its own recipe.

Make up your own giant thing. Imagine many tiny bubbles joining into one bubble as big as your classroom. What would you say might happen next?

board.text: Many tiny bubbles → one giant bubble

text.en: Which sound word would you pick when your giant bubble bursts? Try saying pop quietly, and then say it in a voice that fits something very big.
Say plate, clap and blue slowly. Move from the first sound straight into the l sound, then say the whole word again at your usual speed.

board.text: plate: pl | clap: cl | blue: bl

text.en: With a grown-up, fold foil into a little boat and float it in a bowl. Predict what happens if you press the sides down and water gets inside. Then watch and describe the result.
Describe a harvest meal in two sentences. Say what one dish is made from, then choose a word such as soft, savoury or warm to help your listener imagine it.

problem.en: Match the animals: a cock and a ___ . Choose hen or cow.

text.en: A cock is a male bird.

why.en: We look for the female of the same kind of bird.

text.en: The female bird is the hen.

why.en: Cow is the female of the bull, not of the cock.

text.en: So a cock goes with a hen.

why.en: Pairs are the male and female of the same animal.

problem.en: Which is most likely to float: a dry feather, a small stone or a solid metal spoon?

text.en: Predict what will happen, then place the objects gently on water to test your prediction with a grown-up.

why.en: The material and shape of each object matter.

text.en: A dry feather usually stays on the surface at first.

why.en: We say it floats while it is on the surface.

text.en: The stone and solid metal spoon will usually go to the bottom.

why.en: We say an object sinks when it goes below the surface and down to the bottom.

prompt.en: Tell a friend what the poem is about and why it is funny.

requiredIdeas.en: Many small things become one big thing
Big laddoo, big child, big sea
The big child throws the laddoo and makes a splish-splash

commonMisconceptions.en: The poem is about a real giant

points.en: The poem imagines laddoos, children and seas becoming one big one.
Cl, pl and bl are blends that start many words.
A cock goes with a hen, a lion with a lioness, a peacock with a peahen.
An object's material and shape affect whether it floats or sinks.
